files.content:
name: Preflight — verify /cmd endpoint

# Builds the system-manager config into a bootable VM image and confirms
# that computer-server (/cmd on port 8000) comes up before any consumer
# of this flake picks up the new revision.
#
# Triggered on every push to main and every PR. The cloud image build
# workflow (build-kubevirt-linux-container-disk.yml) pins this repo via
# the Nix flake, so a green preflight here is the quality gate for the
# image.

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:

concurrency:
  group: preflight-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  preflight:
    name: Boot VM and verify /cmd
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30

    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Install Nix
        uses: cachix/install-nix-action@v27
        with:
          extra_nix_config: |
            experimental-features = nix-command flakes
            sandbox = false

      - name: Install QEMU and tools
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update -qq
          sudo apt-get install -y -qq \
            qemu-system-x86 \
            qemu-utils \
            cloud-image-utils \
            genisoimage \
            ovmf \
            curl
          # Enable KVM if available
          sudo modprobe kvm-intel 2>/dev/null || sudo modprobe kvm-amd 2>/dev/null || true
          if [ -e /dev/kvm ]; then sudo chmod 666 /dev/kvm; echo "KVM available"; else echo "WARNING: no KVM, falling back to TCG (slow)"; fi

      - name: Download Ubuntu 24.04 cloud image
        run: |
          curl -fsSL --retry 3 \
            -o /tmp/ubuntu-base.img \
            https://cloud-images.ubuntu.com/noble/current/noble-server-cloudimg-amd64.img
          qemu-img info /tmp/ubuntu-base.img

      - name: Resize base image
        run: |
          qemu-img resize /tmp/ubuntu-base.img +8G

      - name: Build system-manager closure
        run: |
          # Pre-build the closure so the VM can apply it offline.
          # We don't need to actually run system-manager here — just
          # ensure the flake evaluates cleanly and cache the store paths.
          nix build .#systemConfigs.system-manager-test \
            --out-link /tmp/sm-result \
            --print-build-logs \
            2>&1 | tail -40
          echo "Closure built: $(readlink /tmp/sm-result)"

      - name: Build bootable VM image via cloud-init + first-boot script
        run: |
          # We don't run basalt here; instead we boot the base Ubuntu image
          # with a cloud-init user-data that:
          #   1. Installs Nix
          #   2. Runs `system-manager switch` from the local flake
          #   3. Touches /tmp/sm-done when finished
          #
          # We then wait for /cmd on port 8000 to confirm the service is up.
          # This is a functional test of the flake, not the full baked image.
          echo "Using base image directly for preflight boot (no basalt build needed)"

      - name: Build cloud-init seed
        run: |
          mkdir -p /tmp/seed

          cat > /tmp/seed/meta-data <<'EOF'
          instance-id: preflight-001
          local-hostname: preflight
          EOF
          sed -i 's/^          //' /tmp/seed/meta-data

          # user-data: install Nix, apply system-manager from the checked-out flake
          # We copy the repo into the VM via a base64-encoded tar in write_files.
          FLAKE_TAR=$(tar -czf - -C /home/runner/work/system-manager-test/system-manager-test \
            --exclude='.git' . 2>/dev/null | base64 -w0 \
            || tar -czf - -C "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" --exclude='.git' . | base64 -w0)

          cat > /tmp/seed/user-data <<USERDATA
          #cloud-config
          users:
            - name: root
              lock_passwd: false
          write_files:
            - path: /tmp/flake.tar.gz.b64
              content: |
                ${FLAKE_TAR}
              permissions: '0644'
          runcmd:
            - mkdir -p /etc/nix
            - |
              cat > /etc/nix/nix.conf <<'NIX_EOF'
              experimental-features = nix-command flakes
              build-users-group =
              sandbox = false
              filter-syscalls = false
              NIX_EOF
            - mkdir -m 0755 /nix && chown root:root /nix
            - curl -L https://nixos.org/nix/install | sh -s -- --no-daemon --yes
            - base64 -d /tmp/flake.tar.gz.b64 | tar -xzf - -C /opt/system-manager-test
            - . /root/.nix-profile/etc/profile.d/nix.sh && nix profile install 'github:numtide/system-manager'
            - . /root/.nix-profile/etc/profile.d/nix.sh && system-manager switch --flake '/opt/system-manager-test#system-manager-test'
            - touch /tmp/sm-done
          USERDATA
          sed -i 's/^          //' /tmp/seed/user-data

          cloud-localds /tmp/seed.img /tmp/seed/user-data /tmp/seed/meta-data \
            || genisoimage -output /tmp/seed.img -volid cidata -joliet -rock \
                 /tmp/seed/user-data /tmp/seed/meta-data
          echo "Seed image built"

      - name: Boot VM and wait for /cmd
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail

          CMD_PORT=18000
          TIMEOUT=900   # system-manager switch + pip install can take a while on first boot
          QEMU_LOG=/tmp/preflight-qemu.log
          QEMU_PID_FILE=/tmp/preflight-qemu.pid

          ACCEL_FLAGS="-machine q35,accel=kvm -cpu host"
          if [ ! -e /dev/kvm ]; then
            ACCEL_FLAGS="-machine q35 -cpu qemu64"
          fi

          echo "Booting VM (port-forward guest:8000 → host:${CMD_PORT})..."
          # shellcheck disable=SC2086
          sudo qemu-system-x86_64 \
            -name preflight \
            $ACCEL_FLAGS \
            -m 3072 \
            -smp 2 \
            -drive file=/tmp/ubuntu-base.img,if=virtio,format=qcow2,snapshot=on \
            -drive file=/tmp/seed.img,if=virtio,format=raw \
            -netdev user,id=net0,hostfwd=tcp::${CMD_PORT}-:8000 \
            -device virtio-net-pci,netdev=net0 \
            -serial file:"$QEMU_LOG" \
            -display none \
            -daemonize \
            -pidfile "$QEMU_PID_FILE"

          QEMU_PID=$(cat "$QEMU_PID_FILE")
          echo "QEMU PID: $QEMU_PID"

          cleanup() {
            echo "--- preflight cleanup ---"
            sudo kill "$QEMU_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
            echo "::group::QEMU serial console (last 150 lines)"
            tail -n 150 "$QEMU_LOG" 2>/dev/null || true
            echo "::endgroup::"
          }
          trap cleanup EXIT

          echo "Waiting up to ${TIMEOUT}s for POST http://localhost:${CMD_PORT}/cmd ..."
          DEADLINE=$(( $(date +%s) + TIMEOUT ))
          ATTEMPT=0
          while true; do
            ATTEMPT=$(( ATTEMPT + 1 ))
            if [ "$(date +%s)" -ge "$DEADLINE" ]; then
              echo "TIMEOUT: /cmd did not respond within ${TIMEOUT}s"
              exit 1
            fi

            HTTP_CODE=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" \
              --max-time 5 \
              -X POST "http://localhost:${CMD_PORT}/cmd" \
              -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
              -d '{}' 2>/dev/null || echo "000")

            echo "[$(date -u +%H:%M:%S)] attempt ${ATTEMPT} — HTTP ${HTTP_CODE}"

            # Any non-5xx, non-connection-error response means computer-server is up.
            # A 400/422 (bad request body) is fine — the service is listening.
            if [ "$HTTP_CODE" != "000" ] && [ "$HTTP_CODE" -lt 500 ]; then
              echo "PASS: /cmd responded with HTTP ${HTTP_CODE} — computer-server is up"
              break
            fi

            sleep 10
          done

          echo "Preflight passed."
